items.title: Lab 04: A* Search Algorithm for Romania Route Finding
items.description: Implement A* search to find the shortest route from Arad to Bucharest on the Romania map. Use straight-line distance to Bucharest as the heuristic. Print the path, its cost and the order in which nodes are expanded.

attachments.title: Lab04_AStar_Handout.pdf
attachments.text:
A* Search

A* evaluates nodes with f(n) = g(n) + h(n), where g(n) is the path cost from the start to n and h(n) is the estimated cost from n to the goal.

Algorithm:
1. Put the start node on the frontier (a priority queue ordered by f).
2. Pop the node with the lowest f. If it is the goal, return the path.
3. Otherwise expand it: for each neighbour compute g = g(parent) + step cost and f = g + h. Add or update it on the frontier if this g is better than any seen before.
4. Repeat until the frontier is empty.

Admissible heuristic: never overestimates the true cost to the goal. With an admissible heuristic, tree-search A* is optimal.
Consistent (monotone) heuristic: h(n) <= c(n, n') + h(n') for every successor n'. Consistency implies admissibility and makes graph-search A* optimal.

Straight-line distances to Bucharest: Arad 366, Sibiu 253, Rimnicu Vilcea 193, Fagaras 176, Pitesti 100, Timisoara 329, Zerind 374, Bucharest 0.
Road costs: Arad-Sibiu 140, Arad-Timisoara 118, Arad-Zerind 75, Sibiu-Fagaras 99, Sibiu-Rimnicu Vilcea 80, Rimnicu Vilcea-Pitesti 97, Pitesti-Bucharest 101, Fagaras-Bucharest 211.

Expected result: Arad -> Sibiu -> Rimnicu Vilcea -> Pitesti -> Bucharest, cost 418.
Complexity: exponential in the worst case, O(b^d) time and space.

items.title: Uninformed Search: BFS, DFS, DLS, IDDFS

attachments.title: Unit2_Uninformed_Search
attachments.text:
--- Slide 1 ---
Uninformed (blind) search: uses only the problem definition, no domain knowledge.
--- Slide 2 ---
Breadth-first search (BFS): expands the shallowest node first using a FIFO queue. Complete; optimal when all step costs are equal. Time and space O(b^d).
--- Slide 3 ---
Depth-first search (DFS): expands the deepest node first using a LIFO stack. Not complete in infinite spaces, not optimal. Space O(bm).
--- Slide 4 ---
Depth-limited search (DLS): DFS with a depth limit l. Fails if the shallowest goal is deeper than l.
--- Slide 5 ---
Iterative deepening DFS (IDDFS): runs DLS with l = 0, 1, 2, ... Complete and optimal for equal step costs, with O(bd) space.
Example graph: A -> B, C; B -> D, E; C -> F. BFS order from A: A B C D E F. DFS order (left first): A B D E C F.

attachments.title: CPU_Scheduling.docx
attachments.text:
CPU scheduling decides which ready process runs next.

FCFS: first come, first served. Non-preemptive. Suffers from the convoy effect.

SJF: shortest job first. Optimal average waiting time, but needs burst times in advance. The preemptive version is SRTF.

Round Robin: each process gets a time quantum q, then goes to the back of the ready queue. Small q means more context switches; large q behaves like FCFS.

Example: P1 burst 5, P2 burst 3, P3 burst 1, all arriving at time 0, q = 2. RR order: P1 (0-2), P2 (2-4), P3 (4-5), P1 (5-7), P2 (7-8), P1 (8-9).
Waiting time = turnaround time - burst time.
